$comment: Machine-readable scenario matrix every SDK integration suite must cover. See SCENARIOS.md for the rationale and for how to add one. Each suite asserts it implements every scenario in ITS OWN family, so adding an entry fails the other SDKs in that family until they catch up. Families: 'server' (node/python/php), 'browser' (js/react), 'framework' (laravel).

scenarios.summary: A provisioned key authenticates and reaches a real resource.
An unknown key maps to the authentication exception.
A narrowly-scoped key gets the permission exception off-scope.
Product create/retrieve/update/list round-trip, archived with active:false through the update route.
Price create under a product, retrieve, list filtered by product_id.

POST /v1/prices/{id} with active:false archives a price, leaves it readable, and re-archiving is a no-op returning the same row; active:true puts it back on sale unchanged. Archiving a product's default price releases the default rather than being refused.

A product's first price becomes its default_price_id; POST /v1/products/{id} moves it to another of its prices (read back, and via expand=default_price), an omitted field leaves it alone, an explicit JSON null clears it, another product's price is refused on default_price_id, and archiving the default price releases it.
Customer create/retrieve/update/delete; DELETE answers {deleted:true} and the row leaves the list.

Test clock create/retrieve/list/advance/delete, with a customer created with test_clock_id carrying test_clock_id (no test_clock key) on create and on retrieve. DELETE answers {deleted:true} and the clock 404s afterwards.
Coupon create/validate/update; withdrawn with active:false, after which the code stops validating.
Tax rate create/retrieve/update; retired with active:false and still readable.
Webhook endpoint create/retrieve/update/rotate-secret; disabled with status:disabled and still listed, then really deleted with DELETE, which answers {deleted:true} and drops it from the list.
A metered price declared with a 12-dp unit_amount_decimal round-trips byte-identical as a STRING. The one case where a client-side float silently corrupts money.
A tiered metered price round-trips billing_scheme, tiers_mode and every tier, with each tier's unit_amount_decimal still a string.
POST /v1/prices/{id} accepts every forward-looking PriceUpdate field, not just active: metadata and refund_on_cancel are set WITHOUT sending active, and the price stays on sale.

A percent coupon created with percent_off reads back with percent_off set, discount_type percent and amount_off_cents null, and a fractional percent_off of 12.5 reads back as the number 12.5 on create and retrieve. Replaces crud.coupon_discount_type_literals: discount_value and the fixed_cents literal are gone from the API.

An explicit JSON null clears product.description, customer.name, webhook_endpoint.description, coupon.max_redemptions, coupon.redeem_by, coupon.min_amount_cents and tax_rate.display_name; an update that omits the field leaves each one alone.
credit_notes lists empty for a fresh tenant and 404s an unknown id — there is no create, because issuance is refund-driven.

A paused subscription is found by renewal_state=[paused] while its status stays active (status=[active]); both filters take a list sent comma-joined and match any value, so status=[past_due,active] with renewal_state=[canceling,paused] finds it and renewal_state=[auto_renew,canceling] does not; status=[paused] maps to the invalid-request exception.
customers.list(provisional=false) returns a created customer and provisional=true does not, with both listed when the filter is omitted.
audit_logs.list(resource_id=...) returns only the rows for that one resource, and combines with resource_type. The 'everything that happened to this customer' query.
?expand= attaches the named relation on a list AND on a retrieve, resolved per page rather than per row, and an unknown relation is the invalid-request exception rather than a silent no-op.

customers.set_vat_number stores a registration, and passing vat_number as an explicit null CLEARS it. The one body where null is a value: stripping it would send an empty body the API reads as 'leave it alone'.

customers.purge without the explicit confirmation argument fails locally and sends no request at all; with it, the purge answers exactly the marker {id, object: customer, deleted: true, purged: true} (not the customer) and the customer 404s afterwards.
api_keys create -> retrieve -> list -> revoke. The secret is returned only on create, every later read carries the prefix alone, and a revoked key is still listed carrying revoked_at.

one_shot_payments.list(customer_id=...) returns that customer's one-off charges newest first, the status filter narrows them, an unknown status is the invalid-request exception, and refunds.create on an unpaid one-shot maps to the conflict exception carrying code state_conflict.

one_shot_payments.create(ui_mode="embedded") with no payment_method returns a client_secret that starts with the one-shot id followed by _secret_, a null redirect_url, a null payment_method, metadata as an empty object (never null) and ui_mode embedded; a retrieve of the same one-shot carries client_secret null.
webhook_endpoints.list_event_types returns the deliverable-event catalogue plus the wildcard, and a type it names is accepted as enabled_events.

tenant billing profile, with a LIVE-mode key (a test-mode key may not write this tenant-level setting): set country_code + vat_id + city, read it back, then changing or clearing the stored vat_id is refused (400 parameter_invalid on vat_id, reason vat_id_locked) and writes nothing, while omitting vat_id still lets city change.
limit < N yields has_more and an exactly-limit-long page.
Auto-paging iterator yields every row exactly once.
Same key + same body replays the same resource id.
Same key + different body maps to the conflict exception.

Concurrent creates sharing one Idempotency-Key all resolve to the SAME resource id and none raises. A loser that arrives while the winner's handler is still running gets 409 idempotency_in_progress, the one 4xx the client retries.

A blank or whitespace-only caller Idempotency-Key is treated as unset: the SDK generates a fresh key, so two such creates succeed as two resources. The API answers 400 to a blank key on the wire, so passing it through fails here.
404 maps to the resource-missing exception with its code.
A validation failure maps to the invalid-request exception and carries `param`.

An unmatched route answers 404 with type 'invalid_request_error' and code 'route_not_found'; the exception follows the STATUS, so it is the resource-missing exception, not the invalid-request one and never the server one. The envelope type and code are still carried on the error verbatim.
Checkout -> settle -> webhook -> subscription active + paid payment.

payments.retrieve(expand=[refund_eligibility]) answers eligible with the full amount and a window_ends_at on a fresh paid charge, the remainder after a partial refund, and the relation is refused on payments.list with the invalid-request exception.
Partial refund books and leaves the remainder refundable.
Refunding beyond the remaining balance is rejected.
Chargeback + webhook opens a listable, retrievable dispute; the open dispute carries reversed_at as an explicit null (no reversed key), and disputes.list(status=[open,won]) lists it.
A SETTLED refund issues a credit note the SDK can list (filtered by invoice_id) and retrieve, with its own CN- number series and parts summing to its total.
invoices.void on a PAID invoice maps to the conflict exception carrying code invoice_not_voidable: voiding claims a sale was never owed, which is false once money moved.
A usage record posts to a metered subscription; replaying the same Idempotency-Key returns the same record.
Listing with invoice_id=pending returns the posted, not-yet-invoiced records.
Posting usage to a licensed-price subscription maps to the conflict exception carrying code state_conflict: the request is well formed, the subscription's state refuses it.
A second report carrying the same identifier under a DIFFERENT Idempotency-Key returns the record already on file rather than double-billing.
usage_summary reports the pending quantity and the net/tax/gross the next close will bill, so the minimum-charge rollforward is visible before it happens.
A correctly signed payload verifies.
A mutated body fails verification.
A timestamp outside tolerance fails verification.
The SDK's exported event-type constants equal the live API catalogue (GET /v1/webhook_endpoints/event_types, wildcard excluded) in both directions.

events.retrieve on an event with nothing to report (customer.created) carries previous_attributes as an explicit null, and on the subscription.updated a pause emits carries renewal_state with its value before the pause (auto_renew). The key is always present. events.list/iter(type=[customer.created, subscription.updated]) takes a list, sent comma-joined, and returns both events and no other type.

Every mandate-MINTING method is accepted as payment_method on checkout create, and three are refused: directdebit, which a price may offer but which can never be a first payment, plus bancontact and banktransfer, which are not recurring methods at all. Pins the SDK's checkout union to the server's RecurringMethod and to the narrower set the service will actually start a checkout with.

Every method a one-off charge may use is accepted as payment_method on one_shot create (and read back as payment_method), including banktransfer, and two are refused: directdebit, which only collects renewals over a mandate another method minted, and the retired giropay. Pins the SDK's wider one-shot union to the server's OneShotMethod.

A banktransfer one-shot comes back with an expires_at a fortnight out, not minutes: the payer is handed bank details and pays on their own schedule, so pending is not a failure and not something to poll.
The iframe mounts at the configured origin+path and the client_secret is never in the URL.
init is posted only after the iframe's ready, targeted at the exact origin, carrying a REAL client_secret, the session id parsed from it, and the loader's protocol version.
Messages from a foreign origin, and from a window that isn't this iframe, are both ignored.
A real minted client_secret authenticates on GET /v1/checkout/sessions/{id}/element, at the session id the loader parsed out of it.
A secret API key is refused on the embedded surface; that surface accepts only the Checkout scheme.
Confirming the embedded session, settling, and delivering the webhook drives the subscription active.
destroy()/unmount removes the iframe and stops routing messages.
Billable::createOrGetBillKitCustomer creates a real customer and persists its id.
Billable::checkout returns a real session carrying a Mollie redirect url.
Billable::checkoutChargeEmbedded creates a real embedded one-shot for the billable and returns its client_secret, with no redirect url and no payment_method.
checkout -> settle -> webhook -> the Subscription model reports active.
cancel and reactivate drive real API state and re-sync the model.
pause() lands in renewal_state: Subscription::paused() is true while status stays active and the row stays valid(); resume() clears it.
Billable::refund books a real partial refund.
Subscription::billingPortalUrl mints a real portal session url.
The webhook route accepts a correctly signed payload and rejects a tampered one.
